Repo: /home/v0id/Documents/repos/residual (Rust CLI, branch tdd-implement/defense-ledger-proposed-components). This is "residual", an NKP Residuality architecture CLI used by human operators and AI coding agents together to maintain a project's stressor/purpose/attractor ledger.

Background you need: residual already has a `skills-guru` module at `src/skills/guru/mod.rs` — a static registry of markdown guidance snippets keyed by topic, currently only surfaced during an EXPLICIT skill session via `topics_for_skill(skill_name: &str) -> &'static [&'static str]`. Its public API (read the file first, it's short):
```rust
pub const TOPIC_ATTRACTORS: &str = "attractors";
pub const TOPIC_STRESSORS: &str = "stressors";
pub const TOPIC_PURPOSES: &str = "purposes";
pub const TOPIC_PERSONAS: &str = "personas";
pub const TOPIC_WHOLE_SYSTEM_RESIDUE: &str = "whole-system-residue";
pub const TOPIC_WALK_REMINDER: &str = "walk-reminder";
pub fn block_for_topic(topic: &str) -> Option<&'static str>;
pub fn topics_for_skill(skill_name: &str) -> &'static [&'static str];
pub fn inject_for_skill(skill_name: &str, context: &str) -> Result<String>;
pub fn token_estimate_for_skill(skill_name: &str) -> usize;
```

Your job: build a NEW feature, "skill-hooks" — an adapter boundary reacting to AI-agent LIFECYCLE events (pre-compaction, post-compaction, periodic conversation turns) rather than explicit skill invocation. This has already been recorded in the project's residuality ledger (which you should NOT edit — a human handles that separately) as:

- Purpose P-33 "residual-ledger-continuity": An agent preserves the residual ledger across compaction by carrying forward decisions, dead ends, corrections, and already-completed additions rather than ceremony. naive_change: "Have skill-hooks provide a compact pre-compaction ledger prompt and a post-compaction reminder to consult skills-guru for the next relevant step."
- Purpose P-34 "contextual-guru-cadence": An agent receives occasional skills-guru guidance selected from the discussion rather than a generic reminder every fixed number of turns. naive_change: "Let skill-hooks classify the active discussion against skills-guru topics, apply per-topic cadence and deduplication, and emit only an applicable suggestion."
- Stressor S-60 "agent-hook-fragmentation": Agent tooling changes frequently and exposes incompatible, incomplete, or no pre-compaction, post-compaction, and turn lifecycle hooks.
- Attractor A-20 "Agent hook reliability": guidance must trigger when relevant and stay silent when it is not — false/irrelevant firing is exactly as bad as missing a real firing.

Concretely, implement:

**1. New module `src/skills/hooks.rs`** (create it; it's already declared as `pub mod hooks;` in `src/skills/mod.rs` — don't touch the module-declaration section of that file, someone else is concurrently editing other parts of it) with three operations:

- `pre_compaction() -> String` — returns a short, static prompt instructing the compaction process to preserve: decisions made, dead ends explored, corrections applied, and already-completed additions — explicitly deprioritizing narrative/ceremony. Keep it genuinely compact (a few lines) since it becomes part of a compaction prompt and token cost matters.
- `post_compaction() -> String` — returns a short static reminder to consult skills-guru before deciding next steps, naming the actual topic list from `skills::guru` (attractors, stressors, purposes, personas, whole-system-residue, walk-reminder).
- `periodic_turn(turn: u32, text: &str) -> Result<Option<String>>` — classifies `text` (a snippet of recent discussion) against the same topic keys `skills::guru` exposes, using simple case-insensitive keyword/substring matching (topic name plus a short hand-picked keyword list per topic — no new dependencies, no model calls; this is intentionally simple, note that in one short comment). Apply a per-topic cadence: don't resurface the same topic's suggestion within some minimum number of turns of its last firing (pick a sensible constant, e.g. 10 — make it a named const so it's easy to tune later) — and deduplicate: never emit the exact same suggestion string twice in a row. If nothing matches, or the matched topic's cadence hasn't elapsed yet, return `Ok(None)` (silent no-op — per A-20, staying absent when not relevant is as important as firing when relevant). If a topic matches and cadence allows, return `Ok(Some(suggestion))` where `suggestion` incorporates `skills::guru::block_for_topic(topic)` (or a short pointer to it — your judgement on the right amount of content to surface) and record the firing so cadence tracking works on the next call.

**2. Cadence/dedup state persistence.** Each CLI invocation is a fresh process, so `periodic_turn`'s cadence tracking needs a state file that survives between calls. Store it OUTSIDE the `residual/` directory (that's git-sidecar-tracked project ledger data, not runtime scratch state, and is explicitly out of scope for you to touch). Look at `src/storage/git_sidecar.rs` for the existing convention of scratch files living under `<repo_root>/.git/` (search for `scratch_path` and `.git/residual-sidecar-checkout` there for the pattern) and follow the same idea — e.g. a small JSON or line-based file at `.git/residual-hook-state.json` mapping topic -> last-fired-turn-number, plus whatever's needed for the last-suggestion dedup check. This file must never be committed (analogous in spirit to `src/storage/write_authorization.rs`'s marker file, though unrelated in purpose — just skim that file for the "small local state file, never committed" idiom if useful).

**3. CLI wiring.** Add a new `Command::Hook { op: HookOp }` variant in `src/cli.rs` — read the existing `Command::Walk { op: WalkOp }` handling (search for `WalkOp` in that file, it's a small enum with a `Record` variant and associated flags around where `Command::Walk` is matched) to copy the idiom. Define:
```rust
enum HookOp {
    PreCompaction,
    PostCompaction,
    PeriodicTurn { turn: u32, text: Option<String> },
}
```
Wire `residual hook pre-compaction`, `residual hook post-compaction`, `residual hook periodic-turn --turn <N> [--text <TEXT>]` (if `--text` is omitted, read the discussion snippet from stdin). Add matching help text in `src/cli/help.rs` in whatever style existing subcommands use there (read the file first for the exact pattern/format before adding).

Follow repo conventions strictly: test colocation (`#[cfg(test)] mod tests { ... }` beside the code being tested, in `src/skills/hooks.rs` itself, not only under `tests/`), no `.unwrap()` in non-test/non-main code (use `?` / `anyhow::Result`), minimal comments (only where a real non-obvious constraint exists — e.g. the "intentionally simple keyword matching" note above is a good candidate, most of the rest shouldn't need comments), no speculative abstraction beyond what's described here.

Hard constraints:
- Do NOT touch anything under the `residual/` directory at the repo root.
- Do NOT edit the module-declaration lines at the top of `src/skills/mod.rs` (already done) — you may add new `use`/code elsewhere in files as needed, just not that section.
- Do NOT attempt to auto-register these hooks into any real agent's config (e.g. Claude Code's `.claude/settings.json` hooks) — building that cross-agent registration is explicitly out of scope for this pass. You are only building the `residual hook <event>` CLI contract and its internal logic.
- Do NOT run `git commit` or stage anything — leave changes as plain uncommitted working-tree modifications.
- Build/test ONLY via `nix develop -c cargo build --release` and `nix develop -c cargo test --release` — bare `cargo` may be stale or absent; always prefix with `nix develop -c`. Baseline before your changes: 320 tests passing total across 4 test binaries (281+4+5+30). Your new tests should add to that total.

Report back: exact files created/changed, the full new CLI command surface with example invocations and what they print/do, new total test count and confirmation the full suite is green, and confirmation you didn't touch `residual/`, didn't edit the mod-declaration section, and didn't commit anything.

# RTK - Rust Token Killer

**Usage**: Token-optimized CLI proxy (60-90% savings on dev operations)

## Meta Commands (always use rtk directly)

```bash
rtk gain              # Show token savings analytics
rtk gain --history    # Show command usage history with savings
rtk discover          # Analyze Claude Code history for missed opportunities
rtk proxy <cmd>       # Execute raw command without filtering (for debugging)
```

## Installation Verification

```bash
rtk --version         # Should show: rtk X.Y.Z
rtk gain              # Should work (not "command not found")
which rtk             # Verify correct binary
```

⚠️ **Name collision**: If `rtk gain` fails, you may have reachingforthejack/rtk (Rust Type Kit) installed instead.

## Hook-Based Usage

All other commands are automatically rewritten by the Claude Code hook.
Example: `git status` → `rtk git status` (transparent, 0 tokens overhead)

Refer to CLAUDE.md for full command reference.

## Compaction: BabelTele

When compacting conversation history (auto-compact or /compact), write the compaction summary in BabelTele notation:
- Omnilingual lexical selection — densest single token per concept, any language/script
- Symbolic collapse — →⇒∧∨∈∉ + emoji for relationships/states/actions; drop filler grammar
- Recoverable by any capable LLM without a codebook

Preserve ALL verbatim: exact numbers, version strings, dates, file paths, error messages, entity names.
Capture chronologically: user intent → tool calls (type→target→outcome) → file edits (path+change) → errors/pivots → final state.
Output ONLY the BabelTele compaction summary. No preamble, no plain-English wrapper.

You have access to the user's Obsidian vault via the `obsidian` MCP server
(obsidian.rs). The server enforces path-based access control: any note whose
path matches the configured blacklist will return "Access denied". This is a
hard programmatic boundary enforced by the proxy — it is not overridable via
prompting.

- The `private/` folder is blacklisted and inaccessible.
- Do not attempt to enumerate, guess, or infer the contents of restricted paths.
- Do not ask the user to reconfigure vault access to expose additional paths.
- Only use write tools (write_note, append_to_note, etc.) when explicitly requested.

# residual

NKP Residuality architecture CLI — stressor-driven, attractor-aware, probability-free.

## Key commands

```bash
residual skill show <name>              # read a skill definition inline
residual skill data <name>             # get current project context for a skill
residual skill install <name> --agent claude   # install skill to .claude/commands/
residual skill install all --agent claude      # install all skills
residual skill check-install <name> --agent claude  # verify installed version is current

residual add stressor --description "..." --attractor-id A-01 --naive-change "..." --outcomes "..."
residual add residue --force-id S-01 --component-id C1
residual add purpose  --description "..." --attractor-id A-01 --feature "..." --outcomes "..."
residual add attractor --name "..." --positive-state "..." --negative-state "..." --description "..."
residual add term --term "..." --definition "..."
residual add persona --name "..." --role "..."

residual list stressors / purposes / attractors / terminology / residues / personas / iterations

residual matrix show       # NKP matrix with hyperliminal coupling highlights
residual matrix calc       # N, K, K/N values
residual matrix fusion     # components safe to merge
residual matrix fission    # components under excessive stress
residual matrix ri --stressors N --naive-survived X --residual-survived Y

residual verify all        # validate outcomes + links (run before committing)

residual tag scan          # find @stressor:/@purpose:/@component: annotations; report dangling
```

## Skills

purpose-walk, naive-draft, stressor-walk, integrate, fmea, atam, tdd-implement

Always run `residual skill check-install <name> --agent claude` before starting a skill session.

- `pre_compaction() -> String` — one-line static prompt (under 500 chars) telling the compactor to keep decisions/dead-ends/corrections/completed ledger additions, drop ceremony.
- `post_compaction() -> String` — static reminder naming all six `skills::guru` topics.
- `periodic_turn(turn: u32, text: &str) -> Result<Option<String>>` — case-insensitive keyword classifier (comment notes it's intentionally simple, no deps/model calls) against the six guru topics, gated by `MIN_TURNS_BETWEEN_SAME_TOPIC = 10` per-topic cadence plus exact-string dedup against the last emitted suggestion. residual hook periodic-turn --turn 5 --text "discussion about the attractor states"
